text: Comms panel (rescue): headline '28.8 M / 17.1 s for this hole', 'REDSHIFT 1+Z 1.082', 'APPEARS AT 9.51 rs' - three unexplained units in the first screenful; the explanation of rs and M is below the fold. The 'CAPSULE - WHAT YOU SEE' diagram shows the horizon and the station but no visible capsule marker, so it is unclear what I am looking at.

Comms capsule diagram: the capsule is a glowing dot next to the labelled 'station' marker, but the dot itself has no label and changes colour (green -> yellow) as it falls with no legend. Horizon and station are labelled; the thing I am trying to save is not. Also, once I scroll down to read Ines's messages, the Fire recall beam button scrolls out of view during a time-critical decision.

Helm console: the left 3D half of the screen goes solid black (no ship, no windows, no black hole) for as long as the helm panel is open; waited 3+ s and re-shot, still black. Other consoles (comms) show the console screen and the black hole there. The helm panel itself is one line ('Holding station at 10 rs. Descent is locked until the survey plan calls for it.'), with no hint of what the survey plan is or where to find it. Also the hamburger menu button overlaps the 'Esc or Q to step back' hint.

Probe console: the in-world screen says 'ORPHEUS locked' while the side panel shows a 'Launch Orpheus' button (dimmed orange, no text saying it is locked or why). Mixed message: is it available or not? 'Erebus' is used as a name with no reminder that it is the black hole. 'K-1 spent' with no explanation.

Spacetime map panel 'Ines's fall': caption says 'The gold line is the probe' but the panel's plot (window 't 131-181 M') has no gold line at all, only the station line and two green signal lines; the fall has scrolled off the left. The in-world screen behind it DOES show the gold line hitting the singularity. So the title says Ines, the caption says probe, and the plot shows neither. Also the caption mentions light cones whose edge 'lies flat' at the horizon, but no cones are drawn at the horizon row. Axis label 't-hat' and 'r = 0' are unexplained.

Spacetime map wall screen: faint large text ('III The des...' and a smaller line) shows through / behind the in-world SPACETIME MAP screen, as if another screen or a chapter title is z-fighting with it. Also the 'Progress saved' toast covers the panel's caption text bottom right.

After a successful rescue (WREN: 'Beam delivered, in time', Ines: 'I'm climbing'), the in-world wall screen 'SPACETIME MAP - capsule' draws a gold line diving through the horizon and ending on the singularity (r = 0). To a non-physicist this reads as 'Ines died'. Combined with the panel caption calling the gold line 'the probe' and the panel title 'Ines's fall', I could not tell whose path that is. The wall screen and the panel also show different time windows (wall: 't 113-203 M', panel: 't 139-189 M').

Camera feed console: panel is just 'Camera feed / No signal.' with no hint what will feed it (the Orpheus camera probe, later) or when. A one-line 'Waiting for Orpheus's camera; launch it from the probe console when the survey allows' would make this console less of a dead end.

Archive 'Two Clocks': the M explanation is good, but it immediately adds 'GM/c3', the playback slider reads '8 M/s' (M per second, unexplained), and the black-hole picker uses '6.5e+3 million suns' / '4.0e+4 million suns' (calculator notation; '6.5 billion suns' reads better). The quiz asks 'When will ping 9 reach the station?' before the player has seen what a ping or the station is in this sim.

Two Clocks result: final status reads 'Gone. The light is stretched more than e^9 times and too faint for any telescope', with REDSHIFT '4x10^3' and BRIGHTNESS '10^-23'. e^9 and powers of ten are not plain language; 'stretched about 8,000 times' would land. The quiz feedback 'Your prediction missed: it arrived at 108.8 M.' says I was wrong but not why (the slowdown near the horizon is the whole lesson). The result is far below the fold; I had to scroll past three readout boxes to find it.

Getting from the lab (archive) back to the bridge was hard: the 'Helm 9 m' waypoint and the nearest 'bridge' door both point straight into a blank wall corner, and walking at it just slides along the wall. I got into the lab by sidling through a doorway and could not find it again by sight; the lab has no signage pointing to the bridge.
